stops.note: 'esteem, public office'; a Roman politician climbed the cursus honorum, the fixed ladder of offices from quaestor to consul
in the Song of Roland (c. 1100), Roland refuses to blow his horn for help because it would shame his honur
the American spelling 'honor' was fixed by Noah Webster's dictionary of 1828, which dropped the French-style -our

current_meaning: high respect or esteem; adherence to what is right
